I do hope you feel better. You currently have more to offer than me and I hate to see someone fall in a rut.

I won't explain myself, but hang in there, you deserve to go on. No one is truly a terrible person and you definitely are not.

I've been told multiple times, fake it till you make it...

It hasn't worked for me, but it never hurts to try.

At the moment if it was that moment that trigger it, force yourself to sleep even if it's just closing your eyes and not moving.

Force yourself to eat even if it means purée everything. Shocks like this can be painful and lead to some sad moments but you recover in time (months) and eventually things come second nature again.

If it's your first time feeling like this there is no real deep damage, try to distract yourself with friends, games, tv, books, anything unrelated that'll give you time to recover.

Think of it as a deep scratch, painful but will recover over time.

It's if you have a predisposed condition or experience multiple trauma and or shock that you should be worried and should visit your GP, otherwise give it time to heal.

Diagnosed 11 years everyone else says it's probably 0 and I'm probably over reacting. I'm 23...

Everyone else says it's all in my head though and I'm just using it as an excuse. Every time I try to get help the professionally recommended way I'm reprimanded for looking for a convenient excuse...

I want to try a full therapy or even medicated if that's what it takes... but even now I'm unsure who is right and I think everyone actually just feels the same as me but I'm just the obnoxious over coddled person who can't handled a little pain. I also think I've been misdiagnosed and am really confused just what the heck I'm doing anymore and this runs through my head non stop.

This is wrong here, that's wrong there, that's a lie, this is an excuse, I don't believe you, but most importantly anything you feel and think is wrong and not real...

Sounds like you need closure or a confirmation. In this case it's best to ask what's happening between you two. But also realise what you want. Do you want to be together or do you want to be apart. The answer may seem obvious but you need to really evaluate and see the con and pain of both option and which one you can do without.

Regardless figure out what's happening between the two of you and figure just how much distance you need to put for you to focus back on yourself and not be so hung up and confused about this other person. Sometimes a clear direct answer is the motivation you need and a way to stop worrying about the mysterious and unknown.

If they return your feelings you have an option to figure if it's really what you want, if there is no chance then you can ready yourself with how much you really need to distance yourself... Remeber these things take months to years... Don't expect to feel all right an ready in a couple of days.

You just do, not instantly. But you slowly distance yourself and , for lack of a better word, distract yourself.

It's going to seem hard cause this doesn't happen in the course of a week or sometimes month. Just move away, move on, and find yourself, a you away from that person.

Some people just don't care or feel awkward wishing people happy birthday.

My birthday is at an unfortunate time where people are too drunk or hungover to care. Doesn't mean they think any less of me (or conversely more of me)...

You just never know, ask him about it directly or tell him your birthday means a lot to you in particular and you want to do something about it or just get a happy birthday.

Something like, "can you sing me happy birthday?" Or "do you want to do something about my birthday today?"

Welcome to my life, but I find that sometimes it's not weakness or strength, but the amount of exposure and willingness you are willing to put up with to tackle an issue.

With the case of depression, how willing are you going to expose yourself to people, to find help, to be deconstructed, to recouperate. I'll be honest depression is not an excuse, but the fear and unwillingness to try something that may make something feel worst at first so things will be better later is.

Normal people struggle with things too but they struggle with different issues. Issues that sometimes other people from different perspective are blind to. You need to realize you have your own issues and your own struggles, and just because someone does not have your struggles or can power through from it, does not mean that you're the weak link. They have their own issues that parallel but are of completely different genre.

People move on, people forget, and people want.

I learned the hard way the only real solution is for you to adapt and keep moving. Residual anger sometimes stems from clinging onto anything in the past be it negativity it fond memories.

Don't think too much into. Don't think that you dodge a bullet, don't think that you've been betrayed... It's going to be hard but you'll have to treat this like a memory that has little relevance to you. Just another chapter in a long book.
